questions.subject: Global Pop Culture Milestones
questions.question: Which iconic Japanese arcade game, released in 1980, was designed around the visual motif of a pizza with a slice missing?
questions.explanation: Toru Iwatani famously drew inspiration for the character's round, yellow shape and hungry mouth from a pizza lacking a single slice.

questions.subject: Historical Fashion & Textiles
questions.question: Originating in Scotland, what distinctive patterned wool cloth is traditionally woven with a broken twill weave creating a zig-zag motif?
questions.explanation: Houndstooth (or dogtooth) is a duotone textile pattern historically associated with woolen tailoring and Scottish heritage.

questions.subject: Culinary Innovations
questions.question: What common kitchen appliance was originally marketed to domestic households in the 1940s under the brand name 'Vitamix' or early high-speed blending devices?
questions.explanation: High-speed countertop blenders revolutionised home food preparation in the mid-20th century by rapidly liquefying and emulsifying ingredients.

questions.subject: Modern Art Movements
questions.question: Which early 20th-century avant-garde movement, co-founded by Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque, broke objects down into geometric planes viewed from multiple angles simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Cubism rejected traditional single-point perspective, presenting fragmented subject matter across a flattened pictorial space.

questions.subject: Folk Traditions
questions.question: Celebrated primarily in Mexico, what vibrant annual festival honours deceased loved ones with altars decorated with marigolds and sugar skulls?
questions.explanation: The Day of the Dead blends indigenous Mesoamerican ritual with Spanish Catholic traditions, viewing mourning as a celebration of life and memory.

questions.subject: Theatrical History
questions.question: What major theatrical innovation was first permanently installed at London's Savoy Theatre in 1881, transforming stage design and audience safety?
questions.explanation: The Savoy Theatre became the first public building in the world to be lit entirely by electricity, replacing dangerous gas lighting.

questions.subject: Broadcasting Milestones
questions.question: What was the subject of the very first high-definition regular television service broadcast by the BBC from Alexandra Palace in 1936?
options: A variety show featuring musical acts and comedy
The coronation procession of King George VI
A live theatrical performance of a Shakespeare play
A news broadcast covering international diplomacy
questions.answer: A variety show featuring musical acts and comedy
questions.explanation: The inaugural broadcast showcased a lavish variety bill to demonstrate the new 405-line electronic television system to viewers.

questions.subject: Architectural Marvels
questions.question: Designed by Jørn Utzon, the distinctive ceramic tile shells of the Sydney Opera House are geometrically derived from sections of what single sphere?
questions.explanation: Known as the 'spherical solution', casting all shell ribs as uniform segments of one giant sphere allowed for prefabricated, repeatable construction.

questions.subject: Iconic Design
questions.question: Created by Massimo and Lella Vignelli in 1972, what famous transit graphic design system revolutionised passenger navigation?
options: The New York City Subway diagram
questions.answer: The New York City Subway diagram
questions.explanation: The Vignellis introduced a clean, modernist, geometric map using colour-coded trunk lines, setting a new global benchmark for public transit wayfinding.

questions.subject: Literary Milestones
questions.question: Which influential 1929 essay by Virginia Woolf argued passionately for women's financial autonomy and creative space as a prerequisite for artistic production?
questions.explanation: Woolf famously asserted that 'a woman must have money and a room of her own if she is to write fiction'.
